Bootstrap a spot yield curve from instrument prices

Source: R/bootstrap_spot_curve.R
bootstrap_spot_curve.Rd

Recovers annual effective spot rates and discount factors sequentially from observed dirty prices and dated cash flows. Each instrument supplies one new maturity; all its earlier positive cash flows must occur at maturities already bootstrapped.

Usage

bootstrap_spot_curve(
  .data,
  col_instrument = "instrument",
  col_price = "price",
  col_t = "t",
  col_cf = "cf"
)

Arguments

.data

Nonempty data frame with one row per priced instrument.

col_instrument

Character scalar naming the unique instrument-ID column.

col_price

Character scalar naming the observed dirty-price column.

col_t

Character scalar naming the list-column of positive payment times in years.

col_cf

Character scalar naming the list-column of nonnegative cash flows corresponding to col_t.

Value

A tibble ordered by maturity, with columns instrument, t, price, known_pv, terminal_cf, v, i, repriced_price, and repricing_error. The columns v and i contain the new maturity's discount factor and annual effective spot rate. repricing_error is the model price minus the observed dirty price, in monetary units.

Details

For instrument \(j\), with maturity \(t_j\), dirty price \(P_j\), and cash flows \(CF_{j,k}\), the price identity is $$P_j = \sum_{k < j} CF_{j,k} v(t_k) + CF_{j,j} v(t_j).$$ Hence the new discount factor is recovered exactly as $$v(t_j) = \frac{P_j - \sum_{k < j} CF_{j,k} v(t_k)}{CF_{j,j}}.$$ The annual effective spot rate is $$i_{t_j} = v(t_j)^{-1/t_j} - 1.$$

Each input row represents one instrument; t and cf are list-columns. Repeated payment times within an instrument are combined, allowing coupon and redemption flows produced by bond_cash_flows(). Instruments are processed by increasing final positive-payment time, not input row order. Zero cash flows are ignored. Duplicate final maturities, missing earlier discount-factor nodes, zero or negative residual prices, and nonpositive terminal cash flows are rejected.

This is exact triangular bootstrapping: it does not interpolate, extrapolate, fit a curve, or estimate a least-squares solution. An annual effective spot rate can be negative; its discount factor must be positive. Input prices and cash flows must use the same monetary units. Both the positive finite discount factor and its annual effective rate above -1 must be representable. Rounded input prices can make a small terminal residual ill-conditioned; no tolerance silently replaces a nonpositive residual. repricing_error reports the recomputed floating-point discrepancy, not an independent accuracy guarantee or a convergence test.

See also

yield_curve(), discount_factor_spot(), forward_rate(), bond_cash_flows()

Other interest: accumulation_factor(), discount_factor(), discount_factor_spot(), forward_curve(), forward_rate(), interest_equivalents(), par_rate(), standardize_interest(), yield_curve()

Examples

# Recover a known 1-, 2-, and 3-year annual effective spot curve.
t <- 1:3
i <- c(0.04, 0.045, 0.05)
v <- (1 + i)^(-t)
instruments <- tibble::tibble(
  instrument = c("Zero 1Y", "Coupon 2Y", "Coupon 3Y"),
  price = c(100 * v[1],
            5 * v[1] + 105 * v[2],
            6 * v[1] + 6 * v[2] + 106 * v[3]),
  t = list(1, c(1, 2), c(1, 2, 3)),
  cf = list(100, c(5, 105), c(6, 6, 106))
)
curve <- instruments |> bootstrap_spot_curve()
curve
#> # A tibble: 3 × 9
#>   instrument     t price known_pv terminal_cf     v      i repriced_price
#>   <chr>      <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 Zero 1Y        1  96.2     0            100 0.962 0.0400           96.2
#> 2 Coupon 2Y      2 101.      4.81         105 0.916 0.045           101. 
#> 3 Coupon 3Y      3 103.     11.3          106 0.864 0.050           103. 
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: repricing_error <dbl>
yield_curve(t = curve$t, i = curve$i)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   t         i         v         i_effective
#>   <list>    <list>    <list>    <list>     
#> 1 <dbl [3]> <dbl [3]> <dbl [3]> <dbl [3]>
